Robust and adaptive-shrinkage Bayesian factor analysis (RABFA)

Source: R/rabfa.R
rabfa.Rd

Fits the graph-guided Bayesian factor model of Zhang et al. (2024) to one or more omics views. Each loading has its own Laplace shrinkage parameter; the log shrinkage parameters of features that are connected in a feature graph (for example genes in the same pathway) are linked through a sparse precision matrix that is itself learnt, which makes the model robust to noisy or wrong edges. Without a graph it reduces to adaptive-shrinkage Bayesian factor analysis.

Usage

rabfa(
  X,
  k = 5,
  graph = NULL,
  iter = 2000,
  burnin = 1000,
  control = list(),
  scale_features = TRUE,
  seed = 21,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

X

Named list of features x samples matrices (or one matrix).

k

Number of factors.

graph

Optional feature graph: an edge data frame with columns from and to (see build_feature_graph()), a feature x feature adjacency matrix, or a named list with one adjacency matrix per view. Feature names can be plain ("TP53") or view-prefixed ("rna::TP53"). Edges between different views are ignored.

iter

Total MCMC iterations (default 2000).

burnin

Burn-in iterations discarded (default 1000).

control

List of hyperparameters; see rabfa_control().

scale_features

Z-score each feature first (default TRUE).

seed

Random seed.

verbose

Print progress.

Value

A factomics_results object with one entry, RABFA, holding scores, loadings (posterior means) and meta, which includes the posterior mean shrinkage parameters (lambda), the loadings whose 95% credible interval excludes zero (selected), a BIC-type criterion (bic) for choosing k or hyperparameters, and the log-likelihood trace (loglik_trace) for checking convergence.

Details

This is the same model as run_factor_pipeline(X, methods = "RABFA"); rabfa() is a convenience entry point. Inference is by MCMC: use more iterations (the paper used 5,000-10,000) for final analyses.

References

Zhang Q, Chang C, Shen L, Long Q (2024). Incorporating graph information in Bayesian factor analysis with robust and adaptive shrinkage priors. Biometrics 80(1), ujad014. doi:10.1093/biomtc/ujad014

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiomics(n_samples = 30,
                           views = c(rna = 30, met = 15), seed = 1)
g   <- build_feature_graph(sim$data, cutoff = 0.6)
fit <- rabfa(sim$data, k = 3, graph = g, iter = 300, burnin = 150,
             verbose = FALSE)
fit$RABFA$meta$n_selected
#> [1] 26
